brief.topic: Where Fibonacci Numbers Come From Without a Spiral

s01: How many ways can we fill this little path?
We have tiles one square long and tiles two squares long.
No gaps, and no overlaps.
For a path of one square, there is one way.
For two squares, there are two ways: two short tiles, or one long tile.
Instead of guessing a pattern, look at the last tile.
If a five square path ends with a short tile, everything before it is a four square path.
Every filling of four gives exactly one filling of this kind.
If it ends with a long tile, the part before it has three squares.
Every filling of three gives exactly one of that kind.
These two groups cannot overlap.
Every filling must belong to one of them.
So the number for five is the number for four plus the number for three.
The counts grow as one, two, three, five, eight.
Those eight arrangements are all the possibilities for our five square path.
Add one more square.
Five arrangements can end in a long tile, and eight can end in a short tile.
Thirteen in total.
These are Fibonacci numbers, appearing because every complete arrangement has exactly two possible kinds of ending.
A number pattern becomes a reason when we can separate the possibilities.

scenes.narration:
How many ways can we fill this little path? We have tiles one square long and tiles two squares long. No gaps, and no overlaps.

For a path of one square, there is one way. For two squares, there are two ways: two short tiles, or one long tile.

Instead of guessing a pattern, look at the last tile. If a five square path ends with a short tile, everything before it is a four square path. Every filling of four gives exactly one filling of this kind.

If it ends with a long tile, the part before it has three squares. Every filling of three gives exactly one of that kind.

These two groups cannot overlap. Every filling must belong to one of them. So the number for five is the number for four plus the number for three.

The counts grow as one, two, three, five, eight. Those eight arrangements are all the possibilities for our five square path.

Add one more square. Five arrangements can end in a long tile, and eight can end in a short tile. Thirteen in total.

These are Fibonacci numbers, appearing because every complete arrangement has exactly two possible kinds of ending. A number pattern becomes a reason when we can separate the possibilities.
